stem: A 55-year-old man with resistant hypertension did well on spironolactone but has painful breast enlargement. Potassium is normal. Which change keeps the benefit and addresses the complaint?
A 66-year-old on metoprolol after a myocardial infarction needs a calcium channel blocker for blood pressure. Which choice avoids a conduction problem, and what should she be told to expect?
A 74-year-old takes losartan and furosemide. After a week of over-the-counter ibuprofen for knee pain, creatinine has doubled. Which explanation is most complete?
A 72-year-old with heart failure and CKD takes lisinopril. Spironolactone is added. Which monitoring plan matches the lecture?
A 52-year-old on clonidine three times daily runs out while travelling. Two days later blood pressure is 212/124 with headache and tremor. Which statement is correct?
A 64-year-old with stable angina took sildenafil last evening. He now has chest pain and reaches for his sublingual nitroglycerin. Why is this dangerous?
A 77-year-old stable on digoxin starts verapamil for rate control. Ten days later she has nausea, anorexia and a pulse of 44. Which mechanism is most likely?
A 46-year-old with hypertension has recurrent calcium kidney stones. A 68-year-old with hypertension has symptomatic hypercalcemia. Which pairing of diuretic to patient is correct?
A 70-year-old wears a nitroglycerin patch 24 hours a day. After a month his angina has returned at the same exertion. Adherence is perfect. Which change is best?
An 84-year-old with CKD is admitted with a serious infection and needs a renally cleared antibiotic. Her creatinine clearance is markedly reduced. Which dosing approach matches the lecture?

A 70-year-old with CKD (GFR 24) has worsening leg edema and blood pressure 162/94 on hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, lisinopril and amlodipine. He takes all three reliably. Which change is most likely to help?
A 63-year-old with decompensated heart failure and pulmonary edema has a head injury with raised intracranial pressure. A resident suggests mannitol. What is the main concern?
An 80-year-old woman started chlorthalidone 3 weeks ago. Her daughter reports new confusion and unsteadiness. Which lab abnormality is the most likely cause?
A 69-year-old on lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide has had vomiting and diarrhea for 2 days and is light-headed on standing. She asks what to do with her medicines. Which advice fits?
A 44-year-old stable on lithium for bipolar disorder starts hydrochlorothiazide. Two weeks later he has a coarse tremor, vomiting and ataxia. What happened?

A 58-year-old with diabetic kidney disease starts lisinopril. Two weeks later creatinine has risen from 1.4 to 1.7 mg/dL and potassium is 4.8 mEq/L. He feels well and is eating and drinking normally. What is the best action?
A 59-year-old receiving gentamicin for sepsis develops pulmonary edema. A colleague plans IV furosemide 80 mg as a 1-minute push. Which concern is most specific to this plan?
A 61-year-old on lisinopril for 3 months has a dry, nagging cough with clear lungs. A second patient on lisinopril arrives with lip and tongue swelling. Which pair of actions is correct?

A 67-year-old with heart failure takes digoxin and has had furosemide increased twice this month. She now has nausea, visual changes and new ectopy. Potassium is 3.0 mEq/L. Which statement explains this?
A 76-year-old on losartan and spironolactone is treated for a urinary infection with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Five days later she is weak with peaked T waves. Which mechanism explains this?
